clue.text: Medal winner here

blocks.note: a winner is a victor
this clue's own position in the grid: 1 across, with the numeral written as I

explanation.surface: Pointing at the very spot where a decorated hero stands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' points at the clue's own grid position: it is 1-across, read as I ACROSS. 'Medal winner' looks like one phrase, but only 'Medal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military award for gallantry, a decoration pinned on the bravest.

clue.text: Contend ships (second line) must control one and then another colony

indicators.note: to control something is to hold it in your grip, so the first word wraps around what follows

blocks.note: to contend is to vie
the word 'and' taken as written
as in merchantmen and Indiamen, 'men' can stand for ships
S is the abbreviation for second
L is the abbreviation for line
a second 'and', placed at the end

explanation.surface: A naval rivalry in which a fleet must seize one territory after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'and' sits inside VIE; the second goes on the end. 'One and then another' reads like two colonies but is the word 'and' used twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Diemen's Land was the British colonial name for Tasmania, the island penal colony renamed in 1856.

clue.text: Could this possibly hold your tongue!?

blocks.note: first meaning: the start of the question '... be?'
second meaning: a slang order to shut up

explanation.surface: An incredulous question about whether someone could ever stay quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The '!?' marks both readings: a doubting question and a curt command.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Can it?' asks whether something is possible, while the slang command 'can it!' tells someone to be quiet.

clue.text: Australia: a better protection for us

blocks.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
'a' read as the number one
a better is one who bets, i.e. who lays a wager

explanation.surface: A boast that Australia offers us better protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like a comparative adjective; here it is a person who places bets, someone who lays odds.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratospheric ozone shield absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation, shielding life on Earth.

clue.text: Isn't he a punk with a wiggle on?

indicators.note: punk suggests something wild and anarchic, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters of these words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Asking whether a punk rocker is the one dancing with a wiggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get a wiggle on' is British slang for hurry up, so someone with a wiggle on is rushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something hurriedly matches the idiom of having a wiggle on, i.e. getting a move on.

clue.text: Ahead of a taxi carrying stuff that's amazing to Villa?

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying a load holds it inside, so one word goes within the other
something ahead of another comes first, so the next part precedes the single letter

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi
to stuff is to ram in
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cab full of goods arriving to amaze someone named Villa.
explanation.walkthrough: Villa is Pancho Villa, the Mexican revolutionary, so the exclamation is a Spanish one.
explanation.definitionFit: ¡Caramba! is a Spanish exclamation of surprise, what a Mexican like Villa would cry at something astonishing.

clue.text: My mistake: 007's not even involving Q's predecessor

indicators.note: 'not' removes the word that follows it from the spelt-out name
to involve something is to take it in, so the letter goes inside what is left

blocks.note: Bond's number spelt as said: double-O seven
the word itself, to be taken away
P comes just before Q in the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone owning up that James Bond is not up to scratch with his gadget man Q.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Q's predecessor' sounds like the earlier Bond quartermaster; it is simply the letter before Q. 007 must be spelt out as it is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is the exclamation one gives on making a mistake, an apology for a slip.

clue.text: Drink to our setter?

blocks.note: surface reading: a toast raised to the compiler of this crossword
setter's reading: the sun, which sets each evening, so this is a drink taken when it goes down

explanation.surface: Raising a glass in honour of the person who set this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' seems to mean Elgar, the compiler; the setter that matters is the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken at sunset, the evening's first tipple.

clue.text: Closets here ordered vests primarily, socks and pants close to hangers?

definitions.text: Closets here ordered vests primarily, socks and pants close to hangers?

indicators.note: things ordered are rearranged into a new sequence, so these words' letters are rearranged
primarily points to the opening letter of each following word
to vest is to clothe, so the mixed letters wrap around the chosen ones
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: the letters of both words
first letter of socks
first letter of pants
last letter of hangers

explanation.surface: A wardrobe filled neatly with vests, socks and pants, close by the hangers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a picture of the answer: wardrobes where underwear is neatly stored beside the hangers.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes-press is a cupboard or wardrobe for storing garments, which the whole clue depicts being stocked.

clue.text: Just this trio of numbers, one pair blending

indicators.note: two of the three items blending are mixed together, so their letters are jumbled as one

blocks.note: NO and NO are abbreviations for number, and ETHER, an anaesthetic, is something that numbs

explanation.surface: A puzzle about three numbers, two of which merge together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is read as something that numbs, giving ETHER; the first NO stays put while the second blends with ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: 'None other' (than) stresses exactly this one and no different thing, the very one.

clue.text: What may be beaten by bodyworker or poser from the audience

definitions.text: What may be beaten by bodyworker

blocks.clueFragment: What may be beaten by bodyworker
blocks.note: first meaning: a car body section hammered out by a ... beater
second meaning: the group facing questions posed by an audience, as on a quiz or discussion show

explanation.surface: Something either thumped by a masseur or asked by someone in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bodyworker' suggests a masseur but means a car body repairer; a panel beater is a British term for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of car bodywork and a group of experts answering questions are both called by this word.

clue.text: Sharing jam, soup, stew or — most likely — deep water?

definitions.text: Sharing jam, soup, stew or — most likely — deep water?

blocks.note: surface reading: dishing out food from one shared vessel, as from a gravy or sauce container
setter's reading: jam, soup, stew and deep water are all slang for trouble, which people share together

explanation.surface: Diners passing round jams and stews, with a nautical twist at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Each food word is also an idiom for a predicament; 'most likely deep water' fits because a vessel floats on water.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means sharing the same difficult situation as others, a common predicament.

clue.text: See 11
See 11
Heralding whiffs of early tea, king given fish to eat has drawn dog

indicators.note: something that eats another takes it inside, so the king's letter goes within
a whiff is only a faint first hint, so just the opening letters are taken
what heralds something comes before it, so the main part precedes the selected letters

blocks.note: given a fish to eat: fed a bass
R for rex, Latin for king
first letters of early and tea

explanation.surface: A king served fish at teatime, sketched by a cartoonist.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Basset is a long-running British newspaper comic strip about a basset hound; R for king sits inside FED BASS.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon basset hound is a dog who exists only in drawings, a strip character.

clue.text: Making fast reaction to red rag waving?

blocks.note: first meaning: securing a boat to a buoy or quay
second meaning, split 3,4: the lowing and fury of a bull shown a red rag

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying in response to a waved red flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making fast' looks like hurrying but means tying up; the bull's reaction is MOO plus RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is the act of mooring a vessel, tying it firmly in place.

clue.text: Crackers? Not one's forgotten

indicators.note: 'Not' signals that the words after it must be taken away from the phrase

blocks.note: crackers means mad, out of one's mind
the words removed

explanation.surface: Someone forgetting whether a person is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Crackers is British slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'out of sight, out of mind', something no longer thought about has been forgotten.

clue.text: Marshal called in live

indicators.note: 'in' places the first word inside the second

blocks.note: to live is to be, as in 'we are'
called on the telephone

explanation.surface: A law officer phoning in during a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like a noun for an officer; it is the verb meaning to put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To marshal troops or facts is to arrange them in order.

clue.text: After barrel-rolling I think we should do some fruit

indicators.note: a barrel rolling turns over, so the word is turned round
'After' sets the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a tun is a large barrel
let's: a suggestion that we do something

explanation.surface: After a barrel roll in a plane, someone suggests eating fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutlets are small nuts or nut-like fruits, so they make up some fruit.

clue.text: Someone who's got off on strips to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
to strip off is to peel

explanation.surface: A traveller who alighted and headed north stripping off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got off' suggests leaving a train; it means having got off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is someone who has dropped off to sleep, i.e. got off.

clue.text: Sanctimonious cardinal has just the thing for repelling wave

indicators.note: to repel is to drive back, so the whole string is turned back

blocks.note: pi is crossword shorthand for pious
cardinal red is a colour
'it' as in 'that's it', the very thing

explanation.surface: A self-righteous churchman with the perfect remedy for driving back the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like a churchman; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide rip is a stretch of rough, broken water caused by opposing currents, a choppy wave.

clue.text: Significant job in bank

blocks.note: first meaning: revealing or striking
second meaning: what a bank teller does, counting out money

explanation.walkthrough: A teller counts or 'tells' money, an old sense of tell meaning to count.
explanation.definitionFit: A telling detail is revealing and important, and counting cash is the teller's work at a bank counter.

clue.text: A pound trousered by Labour source and I didn't intervene

indicators.note: something trousered by another is pocketed inside it, so the first pair go within

blocks.note: Labour is Britain's party of the left
a well is a source of water
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A politician pocketing cash from a Labour source while claiming to stay out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousered' is British slang for pocketing money; the A and pound go into the pocket formed between the source and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave well alone is to refrain from meddling in something best not touched.

clue.text: See 21
See 21
Work with blade cutting down timber

indicators.note: cutting something down shortens it, so its last letter is lopped off

blocks.note: op. is short for opus, a work
an épée is a fencing sword

explanation.surface: A woodsman working with a blade to fell trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting down timber' reads as felling; 'timber' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opepe is a West African tree whose yellowish hardwood is used as timber.

clue.text: Initially concerned, the way dog eats

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: first letter of concerned
how means the way something is done

explanation.surface: Someone worried about the manner in which their pet feeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions flank the wordplay: the breed, and slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A chow is a Chinese breed of dog, and chow is also slang for food, i.e. eats.

clue.text: String of 7-8 horses will do

indicators.note: a string taken from within the spelt-out numbers keeps a run of letters and drops the ends

blocks.note: the numbers written out as words

explanation.surface: Horses in a sequence of numbered stalls will do the job.
explanation.walkthrough: '7-8' looks like a cross-reference to 7 and 8 down, but it is to be written as words: seveN EIGHt.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the cry horses make, so it is what horses will do.

clue.text: Expresses curiosity about group's retiring minister

indicators.note: something retiring draws back, so the word runs backwards
'about' means around, so the first part wraps the second

blocks.note: someone who pries is nosy
set's: a group is a set

explanation.surface: Nosy questions about a retiring clergyman's circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A priestess is a woman who ministers in religious rites, a female cleric.

clue.text: An absolute state, what's 21 of Daley (has nights out with 'Er Indoors)

indicators.note: 21 across means left, and the leftmost part of a word is its first letter
'out' here means disordered, so the letters are rearranged
indoors means inside, so one part goes within another

blocks.note: leftmost letter of Daley
to have is to own
the letters of nights
the letters of 'Er

explanation.surface: Arthur Daley of the TV series Minder enjoys nights out with his wife, ''Er Indoors'.
explanation.walkthrough: In the British TV series Minder, Arthur Daley calls his wife ''Er Indoors', slang for one's wife. '21' is the answer LEFT, so the left end of Daley is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Downrightness is the quality of being absolute or utter, a thoroughgoing state.
